Header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 10:00 PT

Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Marina, Samir, Rachel, eng leads, PMs, sales reps

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Priya: quick state of company, say thanks, mention recent latency incident, set three asks: tightening cadence, clear owner of runbook, headcount clarity.

[00:00] Priya: alright, hi everyone, welcome to the fall - uh - ignite checkin, thanks for coming in on a Friday morning. quick housekeeping, we got 75 minutes ish, please be concise.
[00:18] Ethan: hey folks, i'll jump in with ops and incident stuff in the first 20. recapped the outage we had tuesday night, sorry about noise.
[00:30] Marina: and i'll show a small roadmap slice focusing on cost/perf prioritization and a pilot for Redwood Optimize proposals.
[01:05] Priya: first, a very quick win, team did an amazing job on the rollback, shout out to infra and SRE. i know some customers felt degraded, we want to avoid that.
[01:20] (murmur) Speaker 1: yeah totally.

--- Incident recap ---
[03:00] Ethan: timeline - 10:45pm PT we saw a spike in tail latencies on hosted api for a portion of us-east-1. root cause looks like a confluence: an autoscaling policy that allowed a small backlog, a kernel scheduling regression on the latest runtime build, and a KV-cache invalidation ripple with continuous batching.
[03:28] Samir: to add, the quantized path had a stall under high concurrency. that was surprising.
[03:40] Ethan: yep, the stall reproduced in canary when we bumped sequence length to 2048 with a specific model variant. we reverted the runtime patch and rolled a mitigation to autoscale thresholds.
[04:10] Speaker 2 (someone in eng): are we confident the rollback is stable?
[04:16] Ethan: medium confidence. need to codify the rollback steps and make them a checklist (runbook).
[04:30] Priya: action: ethan, runbook please. make sure to include paging thresholds, who owns what, and a customer comm template.
[04:40] Ethan: yes. will do.

--- Sprint cadence & squad transitions ---
[06:00] Priya: second big topic, cadence. we've been iterating the sprint lengths across squads, some are 2-week, some 3-week; that causes drift and slower cross-squad rollouts. proposing a standard 2-week cadence with a mid-sprint sync for platform squads to reduce rollouts friction.
[06:30] Marina: the platform teams need a fixed window for infra changes so we can do canaries. two-week cadence aligned with weekly canary gates, sounds good.
[06:50] Speaker 3 (PM): does this increase overhead for product squads?
[06:56] Marina: a little, but we'll carve out a 'roadmap slice' cadence for major infra-facing lift merges. product wins still batch into the same two-week window.
[07:20] Priya: we'll announce transitions in the squad channels next monday; managers, please update your team rituals.

--- Hiring & people ops ---
[08:50] Rachel: hiring update - we have approvals for 24 roles next quarter; biggest pushes in SRE and solutions engineering. we're changing the interview panel to include a product manager for infra roles.
[09:10] Speaker 4 (from recruiting): also banding adjustments are live for IC3-IC5 to compress leveling variance. details will be in the doc.
[09:22] Priya: be mindful of ramp time, and let's make offers early for top candidates.

--- Roadmap slice: cost/perf and Optimize pilot ---
[10:30] Marina: quick deck, sorry no slide link in transcript, but key points: 1) model selection recommendations (quantized variant vs fp16) for high-throughput endpoints, 2) batching/caching tuning defaults per workload, 3) Redwood Optimize pilot for 3 customers to run cost regression and suggested knob sets.
[10:55] Samir: pilot idea - enable Intelligent batching + prefix cache for chat endpoints; measure token cost delta and p95 latency.
[11:10] Marina: timeline - pilot kickoff 2026-11-24, 6 week run, report mid-Jan.
[11:30] Ethan: flags to be added to dedicated clusters to allow controlled burst capacity so we don't throttle high-priority traffic during pilot.

--- Dedicated & Private deployment update ---
[12:50] Priya: sales is seeing increased interest in Private (VPC/on-prem) from regulated customers. we need clearer packaging and pricing.
[13:10] Speaker 5 (sales lead): signed an LOI with a healthcare midmarket - they want SOC2 + on-prem testing harness.
[13:25] Priya: we have SOC2 in flight, but the on-prem package needs a crisp install/runbook. Samir, can your team build a test harness?
[13:35] Samir: yes, will allocate a small infra eng pod.

--- Questions & noisy bits ---
[15:00] Speaker 6 (sales): are we going to change pricing because of the incident? we saw a few customer credits issued.
[15:12] Priya: we'll treat credits case-by-case; not a blanket repricing. finance to evaluate impact and present to leadership next week.
[15:30] Speaker 7 (engineer): will rolling restarts be automated or manual? last time it took several hours.
[15:40] Ethan: we're automating the safe-rollback path and adding a fencing check so restarts don't cause kv-invalidations.

[17:05] (brief cross talk, someone laughs)

--- Deep-dive queuing and batching (technical flavor) ---
[20:00] Samir: quick note on continuous batching - under mixed request sizes we saw a tail amplification; plan is to introduce a size-exclusion window for very long sequences, plus model-level kernel preference flags.
[20:20] Speaker 8 (junior eng): when you say kernel preference, do you mean choosing different attention kernels at runtime?
[20:30] Samir: yes, and that implies we need a better model catalog metadata fields to express perf profiles. Marina, can product add a metadata wire?
[20:40] Marina: yup, adding to backlog; we need to keep the metadata minimal.

--- Operational Controls & SLAs ---
[25:00] Priya: we also want guardrails - per-route latency SLOs, automatic fallback to cheaper model variant if p95 breaches, and an observability playbook for oncall.
[25:20] Ethan: the fallback policy will be rollout-only until we confirm quality thresholds; we can tie it to Redwood Optimize signals later.
[25:40] Priya: customers in enterprise tier will get explicit SLA and runbook attachments.

--- People Qs and rituals ---
[33:00] Rachel: new ritual - monthly all-hands lightning teams where squads demo 5min wins. starts next month.
[33:15] Speaker 9: will we record and clip these?
[33:20] Rachel: yes, clips go to #team-highlights and 1 pager to knowledge base.

--- Finance & runway quick note ---
[37:00] Priya: runway and spend - we are still within plan, but Optimize could be a lever to reduce gross unit costs by ~12-18% on some workloads. finance wants conservative take rate assumptions.
[37:20] Speaker 10 (finance): confirm, submit assumptions by Friday to the finance thread.

--- Customer anecdotes ---
[40:30] Speaker 5 (sales): quick anecdote - a retail customer saw 30% cost variance when switching to quantized endpoints; big win for sales to show.
[40:40] Priya: good to surface in case studies later. document anonymized.

--- Closing & Recap ---
[50:00] Priya: recap - three asks: 1) Ethan publish incident runbook, 2) Marina publish roadmap slice for optimise & model catalog metadata, 3) Rachel share headcount and banding docs. managers update rituals and announce cadence.
[50:20] Priya: i want weekly 15 min check-ins for the first month to make sure transitions are smooth; leads, please accept invites.
[50:40] Marina: will share a short one-page playbook for canary windows and a link to the pilot plan.
[51:00] Ethan: will put the runbook PR up and ask for reviewers.
[51:20] Samir: pilot infra tickets will be opened in the next 48 hours and pinged to finance and sales.

[60:00] Q&A rapid fire: several short clarifying questions about canary timing, workload sampling for Optimize pilot, and how Dedicated pricing will be packaged.

[70:00] Priya: thanks everyone. big thanks to oncall and product - close the loop on action items, and let's keep customer trust front and center.

End transcript.
